key_idea: Find a baseline guess scoring 0; swapping positions i,j in it then reveals whether the bottle at j belongs at i or vice versa, exposing the cycles of the hidden permutation with about n^2/2 queries.
sketch: Guess random permutations until the answer is 0 (a derangement relative to the secret, expected e tries). Let sigma(i)=j mean the true bottle of position i is baseline[j]; the swap query on (i,j) returns [sigma(i)=j]+[sigma(j)=i], so all pairs give the undirected cycle structure of sigma: 2 means a 2-cycle, 1 an edge of a longer cycle. Each cycle of length >= 3 has two orientations, resolved by one extra query that plugs one orientation into an otherwise known/zero guess. Total is at most C(100,2)+33+a few, well under 10^4 (pairs are skipped once a position already has both neighbours). Handle a reply of n at any time by exiting, which matters for n=2. Interactive, so the checker cannot judge it: samples_passed reflects my own simulated judge, which was won on 400 random hidden permutations with n up to 100 using at most 2532 guesses.
